text:
alex: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel routing swap a couple of hosts hit OOMs on 16-token batches with kv-prefill enabled. dumps in /tmp/gpu-oom/*.profile

maya: Link to traces?

alex: https://internal/trace/3751234567 Also pasted profiling output: ```
nvprof summary:
  workspace_peak: 12.3GB
  kv_cache: 9.1GB
  decode_tmp: 2.8GB
```Looks like prefill is reserving large contiguous slabs per-request and fragmentation is spiking.

quentin: Is this on the slab-compaction rollout? I remember we added allocator.reserve_for_prefill which preallocates headroom for prefill.

alex: Yup — config shows `allocator.reserve_for_prefill=0.12` in prod canary. Repro is simple: `make perf-run PREFILL=1 BATCH=16 SEQ=1024` -> OOM at iter ~42.

maya: Do we have fragmentation stats from the trace? Could be tiny KV blobs causing lots of slack space.

sam: I ran a frag analysis on the profile: `frag_ratio = 0.34` (34% wasted). Also saw >2000 allocations <4KB created by KV prefill; slab headers + alignment cost make those expensive.

alex: Proposed mitigations: gate prefill with a per-request cap (if prefill will allocate >6GB, fallback to decode-prefill hybrid that only preloads first N layers). Also enable more aggressive compact-on-evict for small slabs.

jia: Quick bench results for the hybrid approach: peak mem down by ~3.6GB, p50 latency +6ms, throughput -7%. Also saw kernel selection change: some requests now pick smaller-memory kernels. Need to weigh perf vs OOM risk.

maya: Important — our kernel selector biases toward fused/high-throughput kernels when workspace >=8GB. If gating reduces workspace it forces low-memory kernels and adds decode cost. Options: bias selector to prefer lower-memory kernel when reserve_for_prefill enabled, or keep reserve but shrink batch.

quentin: Another idea: opportunistic coalescing in recycler during idle periods — merge adjacent free tiny slabs to reduce fragmentation. Cheap on hosts with low util; high risk on hot paths.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll prototype the gating + hybrid fallback. Maya/Quentin can we book a 45m bench session tomorrow to run canary vs control? @maya @quentin

infra-bot: deploy/allocator-tune started by alex at 2026-03-18T15:32:10Z — rolling canary to 3 hosts

maya: Added perf run to #bench-results (id: bench-375123). Observed kernel-choice skew on canary: fused->low-memory path jump to 78% on canary hosts. Will attach full flamegraphs in the bench thread.
